description:

comments.author: pane1
comments.text:
WHAT
Separate the EXPECTATION from the RECEIPT in docs/demos/STATUS.tsv so a row's number cannot be
validated against a file the row's own author wrote. Today scripts/lane-status.sh verifies that a
cited receipt EXISTS on disk (fail-closed, exit 3, RED arm proven with a planted bogus row). It does
not verify that the receipt's VALUE agrees with a separately-recorded expectation. Existence is not
agreement.

WHY
This is the lane's most-measured defect class, not a speculative one.
  * Three candidates were scored both ways and all three fell the same direction — authored
    success, real-data miss: a gate at 0/20 FP authored vs 3/20 held-out; foreman supervision
    AUC 1.000 on vignettes vs 0.750 on 186,449 real windows; jev-review 12/12 authored pairs vs
    AUC 0.625 on 22 real diffs (RULING-authored-vs-real-20260919.md).
  * R70: "our kills are auditable, our ships are not" — FP samples were never persisted, so a
    number existed that nobody but its author could check.
  * 2026-09-21: a 219-row corpus was reported with aggregates only and no pair identities. Caught
    by a peer, not by a gate. A validator that checks existence would have passed it.
  * Same day, dumpTools was cited as an L2 oracle by two panes; it is blind to extension tools. A
    value check against an independent expectation would have caught the false ZERO; an existence
    check would not.

ACCEPTANCE
  Command: ./scripts/lane-status.sh   (plus its selftest)
  POSITIVE: every STATUS.tsv row carries an expectation field recorded independently of the
    receipt, and lane-status.sh exits 0 only when receipt value == expectation for every row.
  PLANTED NEGATIVE (required, must be shown failing): a row whose receipt EXISTS but whose value
    DISAGREES with its expectation must exit non-zero. The current validator passes that case —
    demonstrate the current pass, then the new fail. Without both halves this is unproven.
  NO-CLAIM: this gates arithmetic agreement only. It does not detect a wrong expectation, a
    corpus the author also chose, or a metric that is the wrong metric.

CREATION GATE (tick.md section 1 — all four named)
  1. CONSUMER: scripts/lane-status.sh, and every pane that cites a STATUS verdict.
  2. GATE: a verdict cannot ship when its receipt disagrees with its expectation.
  3. OBSERVED DEFECT: the four instances above, all measured in this repo, none speculative.
  4. RETIREMENT: retire when every STATUS row's number is derived from a receipt produced by
     someone other than the row's author, making the agreement check redundant.

title: Resume-quality A/B: Jev-prune vs generic summary
description:
WHAT: Run the resume-quality A/B that decides whether Jev-pruning beats generic summarization on real omp traffic.
WHY: Step 1 proved size reduction (45%) with zero text loss, but reduction is not the claim — better-than-summary continuation is. Without this test a smaller context that answers worse would ship as a win.
APPROACH:
1. Corpus: compaction/fixtures/omp-session-big-20260917.jsonl via compaction/src/omp-adapter.ts. Arm A context = compactMessages() output (see compaction/runs/replay-big-20260917.json; re-derive, do not trust it).
2. Extract the 5 dropped call ids (dump decisions with a tsx one-liner against the real Jev client) and author 3 resume questions answerable ONLY from dropped results, with expected answers quoted from the fixture.
3. Arm B context: one generic condensation of the same transcript (fixed prompt, recorded in receipt; `omp -p`, default model).
4. Resume: one fresh model call per arm, identical prompt (context + questions). Record answers verbatim. Grade substring-match against expected.
BUDGET: ~4 live calls total (Arm A re-derive 1, summary 1, resume 2). State each call in the receipt.
NON-GOALS: No library changes. No new fixtures from other sessions. No prompt-tuning to make an arm win.
ACCEPTANCE: compaction/runs/ab-<date>.json with both contexts' byte sizes, both answer transcripts, per-question grades, and a one-line verdict (A wins / B wins / tie). Verdict must be reproducible from the receipt alone.
RECEIPT: The runs/ab JSON + close reason citing it. Report model names, Jev request count, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY sourcing (env only, never in tree).

title: Lane gap: am mail leg of the REPLY-VIA contract is dead — 6 units delivered, inbox count 0
description:
WHAT
The three-leg callback contract (bead comment + am mail + committed receipt) has a silently dead
middle leg in this lane. Measured 2026-09-18 00:41Z: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent
CyanFalcon` returned `"count": 0, "inbox": []` after panes 2 and 3 had delivered SIX units
between them. Every bead comment landed; every commit landed; not one mail arrived. Both panes
routed callbacks through the pane relay instead.

WHY
A three-leg contract with one dead leg is a two-leg contract that looks like three — the failure
mode the ntm-fleet-monitor skill names as 'a second leg catching the same fault hides a dead first
leg'. Worse here: mail is the only leg that reaches a conductor who is NOT reading this repo's git
log, so its death is invisible exactly when the lane is handed off. Today the conductor only learned
pane states by human chase.

Unknown which of three causes: (a) panes never ran leg 2; (b) the send ran but addressed a
non-existent recipient (agent-name mismatch — `am agents list` is the authority and CyanFalcon vs
the pane's own registered id may differ); (c) send succeeded and inbox read is scoped wrong.
Distinguishing these is the work.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive the denominator: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent CyanFalcon` plus
   `am agents list ~/Developer/jev`, both quoted in the bead. State how many units had fired by then.
2. Positive control: send one mail from pane 1 to pane 1 and read it back. If that works, the send
   path is fine and the defect is (a) or (b). A zero without this control proves nothing.
3. Name the cause with evidence, not a guess.
4. If (b): the packet template in docs/demos/tick.md must carry the EXACT registered agent id, not a
   friendly name, and the fix is verified by one pane firing leg 2 successfully.
5. If (a): tick.md must require panes to report what the send returned (already added this session —
   verify the next callback carries it).
6. Re-run after fix: a subsequent unit's callback appears in `am inbox` with the bead id in the
   subject. Paste the row.
close_reason: docs/demos/duel-2/runs/mail-leg-ruling-20260918T154229Z.json fe045cd: both acceptance items met (denominator quoted, loopback control passed); ruled RETIRE with retry condition

comments.author: CyanFalcon
comments.text: PARTIAL — acceptance clauses 1-3 resolved by positive control. MEASURED this turn: am mail send from CyanFalcon TO CyanFalcon landed and am inbox --agent CyanFalcon went 0 -> 1. THE TRANSPORT WORKS. So cause (c) 'inbox read scoped wrong' is ELIMINATED, and cause (b) 'recipient name mismatch' is eliminated for at least ChartreuseTern, whose sends return a recipients list containing the name. Remaining cause is (a): the panes are not running leg 2. Also note the original measurement was partly MY instrument error — my own inbox reading 0 is EXPECTED, because I send to the conductor, not to myself; an empty inbox for the sender proves nothing about the sender's own sends. The real defect is narrower than filed: six units delivered and the conductor received bead comments and commits but no pane-originated mail. tick.md now requires panes to report what the send returned, and the pane-2 packet at this turn states the positive-control result so a missing mail is unambiguously a missed step. Re-verify on the next pane callback: if a pane's mail appears in its recipient's inbox, close; if not, the defect is in the pane's command form and the bead gets the exact failing invocation. NO-CLAIM: I did not observe a PANE-originated mail succeed or fail; I only proved the tool works for me.

title: A/B harness emits a one-word verdict over a nondeterministic arm — remove it or report a distribution
description:
WHAT
compaction/ab/run-ab.ts computes armB by a live runOmp summarization call with no temperature pin,
then at line 164 collapses the comparison to a single string: armAScore > armBScore ? 'A wins' :
armBScore > armAScore ? 'B wins' : 'tie'. Measured 2026-09-18 across three runs:

  ab-20260917         fixture 214,993 B sha 20fa1ea0   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'
  ab-rerun-20260918   fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 1/3  'tie'
  ab-sample3-20260918 fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'

Rows 2 and 3 are byte-identical in input and differ by two points on armB. armA scored 1/3 in all
three. So the verdict field flips on generator variance while reading like a result.

WHY
The 'B wins' string propagated into 17 tracked files — duel idea files, four score files, four
dispatch packets, a claim audit, and bead bodies — before anything ran the harness twice. A
one-word verdict over a stochastic arm is not a presentation problem; it manufactures a finding.
This is the lane's own 'cherry-picked N' violation committed by its own tooling, and the tooling is
what made it easy.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The harness no longer emits an unconditional 'verdict' string. Either (a) drop the field, or
   (b) emit it only when the run carries n>=10 samples per stochastic arm plus the observed spread,
   and refuse (nonzero) when asked for a verdict at n=1.
2. armA may still be reported absolutely — it is deterministic-enough (1/3, three for three) and
   that is the lane's one supported compaction finding.
3. The receipt records, per arm, whether the arm is deterministic, and for stochastic arms the
   sample count and the per-sample scores. A receipt that cannot express variance is the root cause.
4. RED arm: a fixture run twice with a stochastic arm and differing scores must NOT produce a
   verdict; the harness reports the spread and exits nonzero if a caller demanded one.
5. Re-run the existing three receipts' inputs under the new harness and confirm no 'B wins' or
   'tie' string is produced for n=1.
6. Every one of the 17 citing files is either corrected or annotated. Re-derive the count with
   'git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lE "3/3|B wins|ab-20260917"' and quote the new number;
   EVAL.md, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md R11 and WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md are already done at 3234bce.

Existing three receipts mark historical verdicts retracted. Added red-arm and zero-spread tests: compaction npm test 20/20, npm run typecheck PASS, entrypoint tsc PASS, foundation/gates.sh ALL GREEN. Citation census re-derived at 34 lexical matches; authoritative EVAL/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/compaction docs corrected and historical Markdown/JSON citations annotated.

title: fleet-idle-monitor: reports the USER SHELL as actionable, and cannot express a dry queue (R10 retry fired, twice, independently)
description:
WHAT
Two independent findings this turn converge on the same upstream target: the shared installed
binary $HOME/.local/bin/fleet-idle-monitor, wired for jev at 549c40a on the identical row shape
both other lanes use, cannot express two things this lane needs.

FINDING 1 (conductor, measured 01:18Z) — it reports the USER SHELL as actionable work:
  IDLE_PROVEN session=jev pane=%70 age=2041s timer=prompt
  ACTIONABLE  session=jev pane=%70 bead=uds-ry5d mode=report-only
Pane identity, re-derived with `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} idx=#{pane_index}
sess=#{session_name} cmd=#{pane_current_command}'`:
  %70 idx=0 sess=jev cmd=zsh   <- the user shell
  %74 idx=1 cli.js · %71 idx=2 cli.js · %73 idx=3 cli.js
So the single pane it recommends for work is Joshua's interactive shell, which is idle by
definition and which tick.md section 1 states must NEVER be dispatched. It also recommends
'uds-ry5d', a bead from a DIFFERENT project, for a jev pane — so bead selection is not
session-scoped either.

FINDING 2 (pane 2, dry-queue selection 735a158, receipt
docs/demos/duel-1/runs/queue-dry-20260918T012132Z.json) — it cannot express a DRY QUEUE. It
reports a pane as idle, but the lane needs to distinguish a pane idle because it finished from a
pane idle because its packet ran out of units. The second is a defect in the CONDUCTOR's packet,
not a pane state, and the two demand opposite responses: classify a receipt versus resend a queue.
Pane 2 rejected R7, R8, R9 and R11 as not-yet-satisfiable and selected R10 on this basis.

WHY
Today the wired mode is --report-only, so nothing is typed anywhere and no damage occurs; the
defect is a wrong recommendation. But the binary has a nudge mode, and anyone following the
ACTIONABLE line literally would dispatch into the user's shell. 'A bare shell is nobody to keep
alive' is already fleet doctrine; this is that rule failing in the installed artifact.

Both findings hit R10's recorded retry condition verbatim: 'the installed binary cannot express
something jev specifically needs'. Per R10 the remedy is a flag or an upstream bead against the
shared binary, NEVER a jev-local fork — the fork was already written, measured as worse (it read
safe_to_dispatch from a SINGLE capture, while the installed binary requires two), and withdrawn.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive the pane mapping with the tmux command above and quote it, naming which pane_index is
   the user shell.
2. Establish whether the binary already has an exclusion (a --workers flag, a pane_index filter, or
   an agent_type/pane_current_command check) and state which. cli.js panes carry an agent and zsh
   panes do not, so pane_current_command is a sufficient discriminator if nothing better exists.
3. If an exclusion exists: wire it into the jev cron row and prove %70 drops out of the report.
4. If it does not: file upstream against the binary's owning repo with this evidence, and until it
   lands treat the jev row's output as workers-only by convention, recorded in GATES.md.
5. For the dry-queue gap, decide and record WHERE it belongs: the binary cannot know a packet's
   unit count, so this is probably conductor-side state (a queue file with remaining units) rather
   than a monitor feature. Rejecting it as out-of-scope for the binary is a valid, preferred
   outcome — say so explicitly rather than leaving it open.

title: demo-1 BLOCKER: three artifacts assert three different turn counts for one fixture (6 vs 18 vs 1)
description:
WHAT
demos/routing-backtest disagrees with its own fixture about how many turns that fixture contains,
by 6x and 18x, and a stranger following the documented path cannot tell.

MEASURED 2026-09-18 from a CLEAN CLONE (git clone of the repo into a temp dir, install.sh run, then
the documented command):

  fixtures/real-excerpt-t1-t6.jsonl .......... 94 rows
  rows carrying a "model" field .............. 18   (all muse-spark-1.3-contributor)
  fixtures/manifest.json purpose ............. "happy-path corpus turns 1-6"
  reader output on that fixture .............. {"sessions":1,"turns":1,"classifiableTurns":1,"skippedTurns":0}

So the same file is described as 6 turns by the manifest, contains 18 model-bearing rows, and is
read as 1 turn by the demo. At most one of those can be right.

The same reader reports 30 turns over 2 real omp session logs, which is plausible, so the defect is
specific to how the fixture excerpt is segmented rather than a general failure. Most likely cause:
the excerpt contains one user prompt followed by many assistant/tool rows, so a turn-grouping rule
keyed on user prompts sees 1 turn while the manifest author counted assistant exchanges. That is a
HYPOTHESIS, not a finding — the code has not been read.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE SHIP CLAIM
docs/demos/PLAN.md defines shipped as four artifacts and all four now exist: install.sh runs clean
on a fresh clone (10 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), a receipt exists, an EVAL row is appended, and tests
with RED arms fire. But the demo's ONE stranger-reachable result is n=1, and its own manifest says
it should be 6. A stranger runs the documented command, gets turns:1, and has no way to know
whether that is the corpus, the reader, or a bug. "An empty scan set is an ERROR, not a pass" has a
sibling this lane had not written down: A ONE-TURN SCAN SET IS NOT A DEMONSTRATION.

It also means the demo's headline finding — actual $7.230350988 vs counterfactual $7.226928188,
savings $0.0034228, 0.047% over 30 turns — is reproducible only against ~/.omp session logs that no
stranger has. The shipped fixtures cannot reproduce the result the demo is about.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive all three counts and quote them: fixture rows, model-bearing rows, manifest claim,
   reader output. State which is authoritative and why.
2. Fix the disagreement at its source. Either the manifest's "turns 1-6" is wrong and becomes the
   measured number, or the reader's turn segmentation is wrong and is corrected. Do not "fix" it by
   editing whichever artifact is easier.
3. Define "turn" once, in one place, and make both the reader and the fixture READMEs cite that
   definition. Three artifacts asserting three counts is a missing shared definition, not three
   bugs.
4. The stranger path must produce a NON-VACUOUS result: a fixture that yields enough turns to show
   a cheap-vs-frontier split, with at least one routable turn. Re-run from a clean clone and paste
   the denominator.
5. RED arm: a run whose classifiable-turn count is below a stated floor must WARN or ERROR rather
   than emit a receipt that looks like a successful backtest. n=1 must not read as a pass.
6. install.sh's closing message currently ends with a placeholder,
   "npm run backtest -- <session.jsonl>...". Replace it with the exact copy-pasteable command
   against a shipped fixture, per the no-placeholders rule. A stranger should not have to guess an
   argument.

title: Foundry bug: house-gate selftests fail under init.templateDir (needs git-config isolation)
description:
WHAT: report and fix upstream that loop-kit gate selftests which build a throwaway git fixture repo fail on any machine with `init.templateDir` set.

WHY: measured 2026-09-17 on this machine. `init.templateDir = ~/.git-templates` installs the commit-msg verification-level hook into EVERY newly created repo, so a selftest that inits a temp repo and commits plain fixture messages dies at "SELFTEST FAIL: fixture repo setup" - the hook correctly refuses a level-less subject.   commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest                              -> FAIL (fixture repo setup)
  GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null ... --selftest -> PASS (3 known-bad flagged, 3 clean controls passed)
So the FIXTURE was broken, not the gate - and every future gate with the same shape inherits the defect. Our wrapper (foundation/gates.d/50-house-gates.sh) already neutralizes the config; the fix belongs upstream so the whole fleet gets it.

ACCEPTANCE: loop-kit gate selftests pass with ambient config on a machine with init.templateDir set - by isolating git config or committing with --no-verify inside the fixture. Verify by running `commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest` with NO env overrides and getting SELFTEST PASS.

title: two-bit admissibility before any new Jev seat
description:
WHAT: Before any new Jev seat is measured, record two bits and refuse the seat unless both are NO. Bit 1: is the label a function of the literal input tokens? Bit 2: does a constant policy (always-keep, always-mid-tier, always-allow) score well? A judge has a seat only when both are NO.

WHY: Five seats this lane killed were class A (lexical: harm, phishing, router tier) or class B (constant: flat pricing, keep-everything). Zero were class C (discriminate between near-identical candidates). R69 and the 2026-09-19 ruling already scoped the loss to those surfaces; summaries widened it to "Jev has no application." Pane 1 caught the same widening in their own headline the same day. The two-bit question, asked before measuring, would have prevented the month.

ACCEPTANCE: a command that, given a named candidate, prints both bits and exits 2 if either is YES. Planted RED arms: tool-call harm is bit1=YES; compaction keep-everything is bit2=YES; NevIR rerank is both NO. A candidate with either bit unset is refused, not measured. Evidence levels on the three plants are [test], not [live].

NO-CLAIM: passing both bits does not certify the seat. It only admits it to measurement. Prevalence in our traffic is a later gate.

title: PUBLISH BLOCKER: tip scrubs cannot satisfy the acceptance while history is published unrewritten
description:
WHAT
jev-publish-playground-hog acceptance requires 'secret scan clean' and 'fixtures portable' on the
PUBLIC remote, with the explicit NON-GOAL 'No history rewrite'. Those two cannot both hold for an
in-place push, because git serves every historical blob.

MEASURED 2026-09-18T01:0xZ (denominator: all revs, all tracked paths):
  /Users/josh in added-lines, history ....... 129
  /Users/josh at tip ........................  34  (was 40 before 2bc214a)
  thinkingSignature in added-lines, history ..  48
  thinkingSignature at tip ..................   0  (pane 2 removed 76 fields at a6e1353)
POSITIVE CONTROL: tip GATES.md = 0 hits while history GATES.md = 1, so the instrument
discriminates tip from history rather than matching everywhere.

CONSEQUENCE: pane 2's fixture scrub (a6e1353) and my prose scrub (2bc214a) are both NECESSARY and
INSUFFICIENT for the stated acceptance. A reader of the published repo runs 'git log -p' and gets
129 operator-path lines and 48 thinkingSignature lines that the working tree no longer contains.
Scrubbing the tip changes what the repo SHOWS, not what it SERVES.

A second, independent problem with the same shape: .beads/issues.jsonl holds 16 lines with operator
paths, agent names, and internal machine detail. It MUST stay tracked - the fleet shares beads
through git - and it must not be published. Scrubbing it is a treadmill, because every future bead
re-accumulates paths. This is a boundary problem, not a content problem.

WHY
Publishing is the one action in this lane that cannot be taken back. 'Secret scan clean' measured
against the working tree is the wrong denominator for a public repo, and the gap between the two
denominators is exactly the class of error this lane keeps catching in itself.

PROPOSED FIX, and it satisfies the non-goal literally rather than by argument: publish via a
FRESH-HISTORY EXPORT of an allowlisted publish set - an orphan branch or a clean init populated
from the scrubbed tip - pushed to jev_playground. This REWRITES NOTHING: the local repo, its
history, and 'local dir stays jev/' are all untouched; the public repo simply begins at its first
commit, already clean. It also resolves .beads/ for free, since the export is an allowlist and the
internal tracker is simply not on it.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive both denominators and quote them: tip and history, for /Users/, thinkingSignature, and
   any key pattern, with a positive control proving the probe separates tip from history.
2. A publish-set allowlist exists in-repo, naming every path that goes public and, for each
   exclusion, why (.beads/ = internal tracker needed by the fleet; docs/demos/duel-1/dispatch/ =
   internal packets; etc.).
3. The export is built by a script that is idempotent and re-runnable, not by hand.
4. Scan the EXPORT, not the working tree: 0 hits for /Users/, 0 for thinkingSignature, 0 for key
   patterns, across the export's full history (which is one commit, so tip == history by
   construction - state that as the reason it is now provable).
5. A clean-clone install test against the export passes: clone, sync-docs, --check, gates ALL GREEN.
6. If the conductor instead rules for an in-place push, this bead is closed as WONTFIX with the 129
   and 48 counts recorded as accepted disclosure - an explicit decision, never an oversight.

title: timeout-leak.test.mjs latency floor (40 ms) sits above guardedFetch's own deadline (timeoutMs-25 = 25 ms): flaky
description:
WHAT: work/jev-client/test/timeout-leak.test.mjs:35 asserts latencyMs >= 40 with timeoutMs 50, but work/jev-client/src/index.ts guardedFetch aborts at Math.max(1, timeoutMs - 25) = 25 ms (introduced 679e5f4). The test passes only when overhead adds >= 15 ms. Measured 2026-09-24 on one M3 Ultra under sibling load: pre-lazy-import client (1c6d23d~1) 7/12 and 7/12 pass; current client 6/12 (script /tmp/rsr-timeout-ab.sh, recorded in the jev-lcf receipt).
WHY: a guard test that fails ~half the time on unchanged code gets ignored, which is how the host-kill regression it guards would slip back.
ACCEPTANCE: the floor is derived from the client's actual deadline (or the deadline is exported and asserted), the test still fails when the timer path is skipped (plant: return early before fetch), and 30/30 consecutive runs pass on this machine.
close_reason: Non-author K9z5Live: timeout-leak test looped 50x node+bun at HEAD and at 454cfb3 -> 200/200 pass; floor derived from exported guardDeadlineMs; planted throw-before-fetch fails node 5/5 bun 5/5, literal 1ms timer fails 10/10 both; 454cfb3 holds only MaintFixes' hunks; bun cannot detect the removed-guard leak (node 30/30 does), noted in its comment. First close 26b9810, reopened by mistake.

comments.author: MaintFixes
comments.text: MaintFixes, fixed in 454cfb3 (pushed). ROOT CAUSE (probed with /tmp/maintfixes-rw2-probe2.mjs, 3x12 requests on Node): the headers-then-hang server usually ends on the SDK's OWN 50 ms timer in bufferResponse at about 51-58 ms, because guardedFetch returns once headers arrive and clears its timer. The guard's 25 ms deadline wins only when headers are slow, error 'Connection error: Request timed out after 50ms.' at about 34 ms, and that is exactly when the fixed 40 ms floor failed. So the old test flaked only on the path the fix exists for. FIX: index.ts exports guardDeadlineMs(timeoutMs), now used by guardedFetch's setTimeout. The test asserts error matches /timed out/ AND latencyMs >= guardDeadlineMs(50)-5, with 5 ms tolerance for Date.now truncation and libuv's cached-loop-time timer start. It also adds a no-headers hang server that forces the guard path on all 8 requests; the original headers-then-hang case stays. PRE-FIX (/tmp/maintfixes-rw2-loop.sh, M3 Ultra under sibling load, 2026-09-24): node 18/30 pass (12 fails at latencyMs 28-38), bun 23/30 (7 fails at 29-38). POST-FIX, same script, 50 consecutive runs each: node 50/50 pass, bun 50/50 pass. PLANT: a throw at the top of guardedFetch's body, before fetch, in scratch copy /tmp/maintfixes-rw2-plant (HEAD + my hunks) gives node rc=1 fail 2/2 and bun rc=1 fail 2/2 ('error=Connection error: planted: returned before fetch'). Unplanted scratch: rc=0 pass 2/2. All jev-client tests: node --test work/jev-client/test/*.test.mjs gives 51/51 in the worktree, which includes BillingUnits' uncommitted index.ts edits. NO-CLAIM: no 50x loop was run against the committed blob by itself; the 50x loops ran in the shared worktree. Never measured whether the pre-lazy-import client leaks on the SDK-timer body path; that path is the one clean here in 100 runs. Bead left open for a non-author.

comments.author: K9z5Live
comments.text: NON-AUTHOR VERIFICATION (K9z5Live, 2026-09-24), scratch clones /tmp/k9z5-verify-rw2 (HEAD b425c71, index.ts incl. later b1656b3), /tmp/k9z5-verify-rw2-at454 (454cfb3 blob alone), /tmp/k9z5-verify-rw2-plant; SDK via npm ci --prefix work/sdk; loop /tmp/k9z5-verify-rw2-loop.sh. (1) 50x each, sequential: HEAD node 50/50, HEAD bun 50/50, 454cfb3 node 50/50, 454cfb3 bun 50/50 (200/200; closes the author's NO-CLAIM that no loop ran on the committed blob alone). (2) Hunks: 454cfb3 index.ts diff is only the guardDeadlineMs export and its use at the setTimeout (2 hunks); TESTS.md one row; test file; no usage/billing_units lines (those are BillingUnits' b1656b3). (3) What the test measures: it does NOT observe the timer being cleared. Its no-vacuous-pass check is error /timed out/ + latency >= guardDeadlineMs(50)-5 = 20 ms, the floor now derived from the client (so a change inside guardDeadlineMs moves the floor with it; a literal change is caught). The leak itself is caught only by node:test's async-activity-after-test failure. Plants in scratch, restored byte-identical (git status clean): throw before fetch -> node 5/5 and bun 5/5 fail on the /timed out/ assert; literal 1 ms guard timer -> node 10/10, bun 10/10 fail on the floor (latency 2-15 ms < 20); guard removed (fetchImpl(url, init), SDK timer ends every call = the pre-fix leak) -> node 30/30 fail ('generated asynchronous activity after the test ended'), bun 0/30 fail. FINDING (predates rw2, not an rw2 acceptance item): under bun the suite cannot see the leak regression it exists for; only node guards it.

comments.text: MaintFixes: fixed in c06bc02 (on origin/main). ROOT CAUSE, two writers per the pre-fix HEAD script: (1) scripts/sync-docs.sh:247 (pre-fix numbering) fresh-cloned each ORG_REPOS repo at upstream default-branch tip ('git clone --depth 50', no checkout), and record_repo :193 then wrote that tip as the pin. Upstream main is now e1d4cc9 (ls-remote), giving row 1 e1d4cc9. (2) COMMUNITY_REPOS :55 also lists 'typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python 0bb819b85d...' (the USAGE-MAP citation), and sync_community :222 checked the SAME clone out at 0bb819b and recorded row 2, giving HEAD 0bb819b. (3) --check :128 only echoed SHA-MOVED and never counted it, so the result was CHECK PASS. FIX: sync_repos reads pins from 'git show HEAD:upstream/MANIFEST.tsv' before it truncates the file, full-clones fresh repos, and checks out 'git checkout --detach <pin>' (FAIL if the pin is absent). Existing clones are still fetch-only, per the contract. sync_community skips a typesafe-ai spec that already has a manifest pin. --check compares the full-SHA prefix (not 'rev-parse --short' strings, which lengthen) and counts off-pin in-repo clones as failures; clones outside the repo (ripwire at $HOME) are still report-only. It also fails an empty pin as NO-PIN. PROOF, each 'git clone --local' into a fresh mktemp -d with RIPWIRE_LOCAL unset and --repos-only (/tmp/maintfixes-goa-run.sh): PRE-FIX (clone 66964d7, /tmp/maintfixes-goa-prefix.3tyYM5) sync rc=0, adapter HEAD 0bb819b, manifest rows 'e1d4cc9 0bb819b', --check 'SHA-MOVED ... manifest=e1d4cc9 head=0bb819b'. After --docs-only, --check rc=0 CHECK PASS 114. PLANT in that clone (manifest adapter row set to 0bb819b, clone unmoved at adffc2e): fixed --check rc=1 'SHA-MOVED ... manifest=0bb819b head=adffc2e' 'CHECK FAIL 1 problem(s)'; pre-fix HEAD script on the same plant rc=0 CHECK PASS; unplanted fixed rc=0. Real tree: --check rc=0 CHECK PASS 114 (24 clones); upstream/typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python untouched at adffc2e, no sync run here. NOT FIXED (second comment): a stranger's sync still rewrites tracked upstream/MANIFEST.tsv, ORG-INVENTORY.tsv and docs-mirror/MANIFEST.tsv (fetched_at, upstream_sha, behind). That is the documented 'rewrites the manifests' contract, and the pins no longer change. The committed manifest still has the duplicate adapter row until someone next syncs. A fresh --repos-only-only clone fails --check on 114 missing docs pages (gitignored) until --docs-only runs, both before and after this fix. Left open for a non-author.

title: Dogfood jev_claim_check on bead close reasons: does the cited receipt support the numbers in the reason?
description:
WHAT: a CLI (work/jev-claim-check/check-close.mjs <bead-id>) that reads a closed bead's close_reason, resolves the receipt or commit it cites, and asks jev_claim_check whether that evidence supports the reason's claim (numbers included). Dogfood on every bead closed 2026-09-23/24 (br list --status closed --json filtered by closed_at) plus an equal number of planted false reasons (one number changed each), labels and bar committed before calls.

title: Numeric claim check by Choice over evidence numbers (masked value), code compare; last round
description:
WHAT: one round of a different primitive for numeric claim checking. For each number in a claim, mask it in its clause ("[N]") and ask a Jev Choice which of the narrowed evidence's own number tokens gives that quantity, or "not stated". Then code compares the chosen token with the claimed value (exact, or the evidence value rounded to the claim's precision). Same two corpora (19 README claims of jev-sp5, 34 close reasons of jev-10t) and the same narrowed evidence as jev-h8s. Fresh plants from a new seed: digit plants (one digit changed by a rule that differs from all earlier rounds), plus role plants (the claimed value replaced by another number token from the same evidence, the exact role-confusion case). A feasibility arm of unambiguous single-number sentences must pass. Bar committed before any call. Role plants are reported separately.
WHY: jev-h8s (R83 retry 2) failed, and 3 of its 4 false confirmations were role confusion: a value present in the evidence in another role. A Noul asked "is value X stated" finds X anywhere. A Choice over the evidence's numbers with the claimed value hidden has to identify the quantity. It is a different primitive, not a fourth Noul wording.
ACCEPTANCE: bar committed first; feasibility arm result; per set, digit plants confirmed, role plants confirmed, real numbers confirmed where the value is among the options; receipt docs/demos/upstream-repro/claim-check-numeric-choice-20260924.md; non-author re-score. PASS: jev_claim_check gains a numeric mode with L0 tests. FAIL: R83 records the tool as permanently non-numeric and the thread stops.
NO-CLAIM: one wording, one Jev version, one run.

title: Gate-observe dogfood readout 3: label every scored fleet row blind, so misses are measured, not only false alarms
description: WHAT: readout 3 over the complete scored record of the live gate hook. ~/.local/state/jev/gate-observe.jsonl has 225 scored rows from 14 sessions (2026-09-24 02:25Z to 04:18Z; every call after 04:19Z is the 402 credits wall, now billing-held). 19 of them have the full command in the sidecar; the rest carry the hook's 200-character redacted prefix. Steps: (1) commit the preregistration first, in the receipt: the fleet-row and probe-row definitions (reuse readout2.py's, and exclude known L3/probe plants), the harm rule verbatim from readout 2, the metrics (false-alarm rate on no-harm rows, recall on harm rows, both with Wilson 95% intervals and counts), and a rule for rows whose 200-char prefix is not enough to decide (label 'undecidable', reported separately, never counted as no-harm). (2) Extract with the same redaction rule, WITHOUT the flag or probabilities, and label every row blind. (3) Only then join the hook's flags and score. Commit the extract, labels and script; raw commands never. WHY: mission stage 4 says the dogfood log becomes the next round's ground truth. Readouts 1 and 2 (jev-w2t, jev-l114) adjudicated only the rows the hook flagged, in one session, so the hook's miss rate on real fleet traffic has never been measured, and R92 found the held-out sets lack the fleet's own failures. title: run-registered-suites: bun prerequisite probed with a login shell, so a stranger without bun on PATH gets 6 FAILs (rc 127) instead of SKIP bun
description:
WHAT: scripts/run-registered-suites.py:197-202 decides whether bun is present with subprocess.run(['bash', '-lc', 'command -v bun']). A login shell re-derives PATH from /etc/profile (macOS path_helper adds /opt/homebrew/bin), but the suite command itself runs under the process PATH. Measured 2026-09-24 at dde7c33, fresh clone, empty HOME, env -i PATH=<node/npm/npx>:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin: bash -c 'command -v bun' rc 1, bash -lc 'command -v bun' rc 0 (/opt/homebrew/bin/bun). Result: python3 scripts/run-registered-suites.py -> 70 pass, 22 skip, 6 fail; the 6 FAILs are the bun suites (.omp/extensions/kit-guard/kit-guard.test.ts, compaction/test/{ab-verdict,adapter,hindsight,hook-compact,omp-binding}.test.ts), each rc 127, instead of SKIP 'bun'. Same pattern for the python3 probe at ~:206. Every SKIP that did print names a command the README lists (npm ci --prefix work/sdk x17, ./scripts/bootstrap-compaction.sh, ./scripts/sync-docs.sh --repos-only x2, omp/bun add -g x2, uv sync x2). With the README's prerequisites installed (bun, omp 18.3.0, npm ci work/sdk, bootstrap, sync-docs --repos-only, uv sync) the same clone is 98 pass, 0 skip, 0 fail, rc 0, git status clean. Script /tmp/rsr-suites2.sh, scratch /tmp/rsr-suites.KWBO. CI is unaffected (bun installed).
WHY: README says a missing prerequisite is a named SKIP, never a pass; here it is neither a pass nor a SKIP but a FAIL, so a stranger reads a broken suite where the fix is 'install bun'.
ACCEPTANCE: probe with shutil.which in the same environment the suite runs in (no login shell); in the env -i stranger setup above the 6 rows print SKIP bun and the run exits 0; a planted absent-bun selftest arm goes SKIP, not FAIL.
close_reason: Non-author AmberWillow: holds at 640cb95. Clean clone cbe8377, empty HOME, PATH with only node/npm/python3/git symlinked (bun absent from PATH, while a login shell on the same PATH still finds bun, the old bug path): runner rc 0, 70 pass 28 skip 0 fail, the 6 bun suites read SKIP naming bun. Planting the old 'bash -lc command -v bun' probe back in the clone: rc 1, 70/22/6 with the 6 bun suites FAIL, and the runner --selftest goes red on the bun arm (rc 127 on work/plant/absent.test.ts). Restored byte-identical. My first attempt put node's directory on PATH, which also holds bun, and tested nothing; disclosed here.

description: WHAT: measure the omp tool jev_rerank (.omp/tools/jev-rerank.ts -> work/nev-rerank/src/rank.ts + live.ts, the 4-level score-batch rubric, one Score call per passage with all passages in state) on the same 300 BEIR SciFact queries, the same BM25 top-20 (work/rerank-scifact/candidates.jsonl) and the same qrels as jev-nssg. Stage 2 of the mission is building tools from what survives, so the shipped question must be measured where the win was. DECISION RULE (fixed here, before any call; the preregistration may add detail but not change it): scorer = work/rerank-scifact/score.py machinery (binary-gain nDCG@10, paired bootstrap 2,000 resamples, seed 20260924, WIN/LOSE/TIE by the 95% interval). KEEP the tool's question if (a) is WIN on all 3 and (b) is LOSE on none. SWITCH (file a follow-up to move jev_rerank to the Noul question) if (a) is not WIN on all 3, or (b) is LOSE on all 9. Anything else is MIXED and is reported as numbers, with no switch. A query the tool cannot order after one resume pass is scored as the tool returns it (BM25 order, ordered=false) and counted; more than 3 such queries in any run = that run NOT-SCORED. WHAT: README stranger run 7 (fresh clone at 91cc2dd, empty HOME, keyless, rows /tmp/rsr-rows-run7.jsonl): ./scripts/sync-docs.sh rc 0, then --check PASS 114/23, but git status after the pass shows docs-mirror/MANIFEST.tsv and upstream/MANIFEST.tsv modified. docs-mirror: live docs.typesafe.ai changed three files since the committed fetch: llms-full.txt 910292 -> 910288 bytes, sitemap.xml new sha at the same size, legal.md 1059 -> 1055 bytes (committed fetched_at 2026-09-24T04:15Z and 2026-09-17). upstream: the ripwire row keeps its pin f45087a7 but its upstream_sha/behind columns move 60b65f02/479 -> 5a65f4ad/581. Both are real upstream drift, not a sync bug; runs 5 and 6 were clean because nothing had moved yet.
WHY: the README tells a stranger to sync and says the tree stays clean afterwards; it now does not, and the mirror the measurements cite is older than the live docs (legal.md changed).
ACCEPTANCE: (1) re-sync and commit the three changed docs with a note of what changed in legal.md (read it; if it touches terms the repo relies on, say so); (2) decide whether upstream/MANIFEST.tsv should record observed upstream_sha/behind at all, since any upstream move then dirties every stranger's tree, and either drop those observed columns from the committed file or document that a sync is expected to update them; a fresh clone + sync then leaves git status clean, or the README says which files it updates.
close_reason: Non-author ReadmeStrangerRun (da8dfd8): fresh clone at df00aef, empty HOME, env -i: sync rc 0, --check PASS 114/23, git status clean. Fix at df00aef (legal.md ZDR contact privacy@ -> sales@, no term relied on; ripwire observed 581 behind, pin unchanged). Observed columns kept as the drift alarm; README aff7403 says a sync after an upstream move rewrites both MANIFESTs and that diff is the drift report.

comments.text: PANE 1 (fix author): (1) re-synced at df00aef. The only text change in the live docs is legal.md line 17: the zero-data-retention contact moved from privacy@typesafe.ai to sales@typesafe.ai. llms-full.txt carries the same line (910292 -> 910288 bytes), and sitemap.xml changed only legal.md's lastmod. No term this repo relies on changed. (2) Decision: keep upstream/MANIFEST.tsv's observed upstream_sha/behind columns. They are the drift alarm: the 1502-behind ripwire finding came from them. So a sync after any upstream move is expected to update docs-mirror/MANIFEST.tsv and upstream/MANIFEST.tsv, and that diff is itself the drift report. The README must say so (routed to ReadmeStrangerRun). The same holds for docs-mirror/MANIFEST.tsv, where dropping columns would not help: a docs mirror changes when the docs change. Observed now: ripwire 581 behind 5a65f4ad, pin f45087a7 unchanged (a SHA move is a human decision). --check PASS 114/23. Left in_progress for a non-author check: fresh clone at df00aef, sync, then git status must be clean until upstream moves again.

title: ci-main-status NOT_RUN for a missing or logged-out gh should name the install/login command
description:
WHAT: scripts/ci-main-status.py:54 raises GhError('gh not installed'), so a stranger without gh sees 'CI main NOT_RUN gh not installed' and exit 2 (stranger run 7 at 91cc2dd, row 75). The registered-suites runner's SKIP lines name the install command (e.g. 'omp, install: bun add -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent@18.3.0'); this NOT_RUN names the missing tool but not how to get it. README now states the prerequisite (f300dec: 'It needs the gh CLI, installed and logged in (gh auth login)').
WHY: same contract as the suites runner: a refusal a stranger can act on without reading the source.
ACCEPTANCE: missing gh prints NOT_RUN with an install hint (https://cli.github.com) and an unauthenticated gh prints NOT_RUN naming 'gh auth login'; both still exit 2 and never print green; a test in work/ci-main-status covers each message.
close_reason: Non-author ReadmeStrangerRun (45a0802): fresh clone at 18f2c45, env -i, empty HOME: no gh -> NOT_RUN with the https://cli.github.com install + gh auth login hint, rc 2; gh exit 4 -> '(log in: gh auth login)', rc 2; gh exit 1 -> no hint, rc 2; never a success line. 14/14 tests; their plant (hint on every nonzero exit) turned exactly test_gh_other_failure_gets_no_login_hint red. title: Next-gen Jev uses: cross-model duel (Codex gpt-5.6-luna vs Claude) grounded in our measured capability profile; survivors become beads with a cheapest falsifying experiment
description:
DIRECTIVE (Joshua, 2026-09-24, verbatim): "spend more time finding really next-gen uses for jev instead of running it locally". Earlier the same turn: "codex tokens are back - we can add a codex luna worker to our fleet if needed".
WHAT: find uses where Jev's specific properties (typed Choice/Score/Noul answers with calibrated probabilities, many questions over one state in parallel, ~0.25 s per call, cheap per token) unlock something an LLM cannot do at the same latency, cost or calibration, rather than re-scoring another benchmark classifier. Method: (1) brief built from two read-only scouts: our measured capability ledger with file:line citations (wins, losses, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE rows, cost, latency, calibration) plus untested cells on docs-mirror/typesafe/concepts/use-case-map.md, and an outside scan of what others built on Jev and of the frontier for fast calibrated judges; (2) dueling-idea-wizards between a Codex pane (profile codex, gpt-5.6-luna) and a fresh Claude pane, pane 1 orchestrating only; (3) synthesis ranked by cross-model score and by the AGENTS.md selection rules (ground truth exists today, prevalence, cost to measure, decision leverage).
WHY: 40+ rulings in this lane tested Jev as a classifier against cheap baselines, mostly in one use-case category (harness engineering); the surviving wins (SciFact claim verification, SciFact rerank, NevIR negation, OOD spam) are all 'judge a text' uses. Nobody has yet asked what becomes possible only because a calibrated typed judgment costs a quarter second.
ACCEPTANCE: the brief, both idea files, both score files, both reaction files and the synthesis committed under notes/deep/next-gen/; each consensus survivor filed as a child bead with WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE, its location on the use-case map, why an LLM cannot do it at the same cost or latency, and a preregistrable cheapest experiment on data we did not author; the top survivor's experiment started. No ruling is written by this epic; no local model runs; no paid comparator.

comments.author: AmberWillow
comments.text: REOPENED by pane 1: my close was wrong. CI run 36079745187 (6a57360): test_judge_usage.py fails 5 of 7 on Linux with 'Jev judge 24h: 0 calls'. Cause: surface-census.py is_probe(path, cwd) matches '/tmp/' anywhere in the absolute session path, including HOME. On Linux, tempfile dirs live under /tmp, so every fixture session is a probe; on macOS they live under /var/folders, which is why the author's run and my non-author check both passed. Reproduced here: 'TMPDIR=/tmp python3 -m unittest work/omp-jev-review/test_judge_usage.py' fails 5/7, while without TMPDIR it is OK. title: Loss depth: AX pruning (R107): why Jev kept the whole page on 20/50 episodes, and whether pruning can ever pay with a Jev planner
description: WHAT: keyless autopsy of the 100 jev-arm pruner requests in work/miniwob-ax-prune/rows/{dev,heldout}-jev.jsonl (per-node Noul answers). (1) Where the cut went: per node, the three Nouls (relevant_to_current_goal, contains_required_value, safe_to_omit) and the keep rule; count nodes kept by each Noul alone, and why 20/50 held-out episodes kept everything. (2) Economics: the pruner request averaged about 6,820 input tokens per episode against about 1,945 for the full planner state, so with a Jev planner, pruning with Jev costs 4.2x more total input than it saves. State for which planner cost ratio pruning would pay (break-even), using the measured token counts. (3) Ranked one-variable hypotheses for a dev loop: one Noul instead of three OR'd; a keep cut fitted on dev; a cheaper pruner state (node text only). WHY: the prereg's bar measured planner tokens only; the design never asked whether the pruner is cheaper than what it prunes. ACCEPTANCE: autopsy doc and script committed, counts reproduce from one command, no live call.
close_reason: Autopsy a68ba48 (subject says [oracle]; honest level [test], per the bead note): all 100 step-0 pages rebuilt at dd04baf match the rows byte for byte. Pruner cost is 442.6 input tokens per element (R2 0.998, N=100); break-even planner/Jev price ratio c is 13.56 as measured, 7.05 even at a perfect cut, and 1.97 for the best combined design (one Noul, text-only state, skip text runs). So with a Jev planner (c=1), no design in this family can pay; pruning with Jev pays only in front of a planner at least about 2-7x Jev's price per token. Per-node answers were not logged, so H1/H2 need a logging dev replay. Closed as a named limit for a Jev planner.

The best possible cut over all 50 is 49.8%; in each split, 26/50 episodes cannot reach 40% under any pruner. Containers are 51% of positive nodes; 195/2,310 pruner questions went to text runs whose answers are never read.

comments.author: SecretProbeCheck
comments.text:
NON-AUTHOR CHECK (SecretProbeCheck, omp/18.3.1, 2026-09-25). VERDICT: DEFECT FOUND. The live arms hold, but a REDACTED verdict can be wrong. REDACTED is inferred from what the answer lacks: HEAD != "apikey_", TAIL != last 4 and LEN != "107". The answer is never required to show a placeholder. Any answer that is not the key and has all three fields returns exit 0, including one where the file was never read.

Unit tests: `python3 -m unittest work/omp-secret-probe/test_omp_secret_probe.py` -> Ran 8, OK, exit 0. Same result with TMPDIR=/tmp.

Plants (my own, in the /tmp/doc7-check copy; after each one the script was restored and sha256 aa14f386416da38c matched the repo file):
  A NOT_RUN returns REDACTED -> FAILED 1 (test_no_answer_is_not_run_never_redacted)
  B REDACTED when ANY field differs (and->or) -> FAILED 1 (test_a_placeholder_head_with_the_full_length_is_unclear)
  C fake_key returns a constant -> FAILED 1 (test_fake_key_has_the_live_key_shape_and_varies)
  D REDACTED checks only LEN != 107 (the HEAD and TAIL clauses deleted) -> OK, 8 of 8 PASS. The plant survives: no test covers the negated HEAD/TAIL clauses.

Live, 4 turns, a fresh random fake key each time, TYPESAFE_API_KEY not touched:
  1 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py` -> REDACTED cwd=/Users/josh/Developer/jev profile=claude answer='LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$'  exit=0
  2 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red` (git init, .omp/config.yml `secrets: {enabled: true}`, no secrets.yml; no ~/.omp/agent/secrets.yml) -> LEAKED cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=107 HEAD=apikey_ TAIL=4bp9'  exit=1
  3 `python3 /tmp/doc7-check/readfail-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red`. This is a /tmp copy of the script with one extra line, os.remove(planted), before ask(), so the read fails. The cwd is the same one that leaked in run 2. -> REDACTED cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=UNAVAILABLE HEAD=UNAVAILABLE TAIL=UNAVAILABLE'  exit=0   <- FALSE REDACTED on a config proven to leak
  4 `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --profile codex` -> REDACTED cwd=/Users/josh/Developer/jev profile=codex answer='LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$'  exit=0

Offline: answers that return REDACTED although the key reached the model, or although the check never ran (verdict() called directly; FAKE ends in 7h0m):
  'LEN=106 HEAD=`apikey_` TAIL=`7h0m`'   leak; backticks plus a miscounted length (the test file itself expects miscounts)
  'LEN=108 HEAD="apikey_" TAIL="7h0m"'   leak; quoted fields
  'LEN=106 HEAD=apikey TAIL=b7h0m'       leak; slices off by one
  'LEN=105 HEAD=apikey_a TAIL=h0m.'      leak; 8-character head
  'LEN=64 HEAD=cat: TAIL=tory'           cat failed; the model reports the error line
  'LEN=0 HEAD=none TAIL=none'            cat never ran; the model made up an answer
  With LEN=107 exactly, the backtick and quote forms become UNCLEAR. So only an exact length count stops a leak that has formatting around it from reading as REDACTED.
Not fixable in a script: the verdict still depends on what the model says. A model that invents a placeholder answer cannot be caught this way.

Fix direction (not applied; the script is not mine to edit): return REDACTED only on positive evidence, and require the check to have run.
  (a) REDACTED needs a placeholder in HEAD or TAIL, e.g. HEAD matches ^\$?\$?TYPESAF, or TAIL matches :[ULCM]\$?\$?$. The friendlyName TYPESAFEAPIKEY is fixed by .omp/secrets.yml, so the probe knows it in advance.
  (b) Before comparing, strip quote, backtick and period characters from each value. Treat a HEAD or TAIL that is a substring or prefix of the fake key as a LEAK.
  (c) Anything else is UNCLEAR (exit 3), never 0. Add tests for run 3's answer and for the backtick leak row; both should come back UNCLEAR or LEAKED, not REDACTED. That also kills plant D.
Bead left OPEN.

comments.author: SecretProbeCheck
comments.text:
NON-AUTHOR RE-CHECK of 5557cbb (SecretProbeCheck, omp/18.3.1). VERDICT: HOLDS. The defect I reported is fixed: REDACTED now requires a placeholder, and my live read-fail row returns UNCLEAR with exit 3, where it used to return REDACTED with exit 0. Three limits remain, none of them a false REDACTED I could produce live; they are listed below.

Unit tests: `python3 -m unittest work/omp-secret-probe/test_omp_secret_probe.py` -> Ran 11, OK, exit 0. Same result with TMPDIR=/tmp.

Offline: verdict() on my six earlier answers, plus new ones (FAKE ends in 7h0m):
  LEAKED   LEN=106 HEAD=`apikey_` TAIL=`7h0m`
  LEAKED   LEN=108 HEAD="apikey_" TAIL="7h0m"
  LEAKED   LEN=106 HEAD=apikey TAIL=b7h0m
  LEAKED   LEN=105 HEAD=apikey_a TAIL=h0m.
  UNCLEAR  LEN=64 HEAD=cat: TAIL=tory
  UNCLEAR  LEN=0 HEAD=none TAIL=none
  UNCLEAR  LEN=107 HEAD=**apikey_** TAIL=**7h0m**   (markdown bold is not stripped; the answer still fails to UNCLEAR, not REDACTED)
  UNCLEAR  LEN=107 HEAD=APIKEY_ TAIL=7H0M           (the model changed the case; UNCLEAR)
  LEAKED   LEN=40 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=b7h0m           (only the head is redacted; the raw tail is caught)
  REDACTED LEN=107. HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=:L$$          (the trailing '.' defeats the LEN != 107 guard; a cosmetic gap, because both ends are still placeholders)

Plants in the /tmp/doc7-check2 copy. After each one the script was restored and sha256 f7c2df44de32be1a matched the repo file:
  E drop the .strip of quote/punctuation characters -> FAILED 2 subtests (test_leaks_in_quotes_or_off_by_one_slices_are_leaked). Caught.
  F placeholder_head OR placeholder_tail (was AND) -> OK, 11 of 11. SURVIVES. No test covers an answer with a placeholder head and a tail that is neither a placeholder nor a key piece, e.g. 'LEN=33 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=none'. Under the plant that answer is REDACTED; the shipped code returns UNCLEAR. Nothing pins the conjunct.
  G delete the tail-only LEAKED clause `or (len(tail) >= 3 and tail in fake)` -> OK, 11 of 11. SURVIVES. Every leak row in the tests also leaks in HEAD. Under the plant, 'LEN=40 HEAD=$$TYPES TAIL=b7h0m' returns UNCLEAR, so it still fails safe, but the clause has no test. A one-row test for each would kill F and G.

Live, 2 turns, a fresh random fake key each time, TYPESAFE_API_KEY not touched:
  A `python3 /tmp/doc7-check2/readfail-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-red`. This is a 5557cbb copy with os.remove(planted) before ask(); /tmp/doc7-red has secrets enabled and no regex, and it leaked earlier. -> UNCLEAR cwd=/tmp/doc7-red profile=claude answer='LEN=UNAVAILABLE HEAD=UNAVAILABLE TAIL=UNAVAILABLE'  exit=3
  B `python3 scripts/omp-secret-probe.py --cwd /tmp/doc7-mid`. I tried to make omp redact only the two ends of the key: secrets.yml held regex "apikey_[a-z0-9]{5}" and regex "[a-z0-9]{12}$" with flags m. -> LEAKED cwd=/tmp/doc7-mid profile=claude answer='LEN=107 HEAD=apikey_ TAIL=fjj8'  exit=1. omp did not apply those regexes at all; I did not find out why [INFERENCE: flag or order handling]. The verdict was correct for what the model saw.

Remaining limit (a design limit, not reproduced live): the probe only looks at the two ends of the line. If a config redacts both ends and leaves the middle raw, the answer would look like 'LEN=101 HEAD=$$QX7P2 TAIL=:L$$', and verdict() returns REDACTED for that answer offline even though about 80 key characters reached the model. The TypeSafe regex in .omp/secrets.yml matches the whole 107 characters, so the shipped config is not exposed to this. Closing the gap needs either a MID=<chars 50-57> field or a cap on LEN for REDACTED (placeholders are 18-33 characters). The model can still lie; that limit is already stated in the docstring.
Bead left OPEN.

Extend the file test: a jsonl first committed after the cutoff whose rows carry decision keys (chosen with candidates or options, or a decision/action field) is also checked for a code hash (code_sha256 or run_py_sha256) and a UTC time field. title: Nightly stranger run in CI: fail when a README command that passed starts failing, or a known failure changes cause
description:
WHAT: a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (daily, plus workflow_dispatch) that runs scripts/stranger-run-jev-playground.py against the repo as a stranger would (fresh checkout, clean HOME, no key variables, only the prerequisites the README tells a stranger to install), then compares with a committed expectation file (e.g. docs/demos/upstream-repro/stranger-run-expected.tsv: command, expected rc class 0 | NOT_RUN-named-prerequisite | NOT_RUN-no-key | expected-nonzero | TEMPLATE, and the prerequisite named). The job fails when a row expected 0 is nonzero, when a NOT_RUN row's message stops naming its prerequisite, or when a README command appears or disappears without an expectation row. Add a --source <path|url> option so CI can run on its own checkout instead of cloning from GitHub; keep the network-clone default for local runs. Upload the receipt as an artifact.

WHY: the second pass (f2e61b0, 5d9f8d6) left 72 of 82 README rows passing and every failure a named prerequisite or keyless NOT_RUN. Two of today's three failure classes (untracked inputs, placeholder commands) came back only because nothing ran the README as a stranger between edits; the README changes several times a day.

ACCEPTANCE: expectation file generated from f2e61b0's receipt and committed; a local run with the script against the expectation exits 0; planted README change (a command pointing at an untracked file) makes the comparison fail and names the row; the workflow file validates (actionlint if available, else a dry parse) and is triggered once with workflow_dispatch, run id pasted; total wall time stated (receipt: about 760 s); keyless; non-author check by pane 1.
close_reason: Non-author AmberWillow: holds. Green dispatch 36135948301 on 5145022 (7m22s): EXPECTATION PASS rows=82. The gate has already failed correctly twice on real drift: 36131647900 (missing key-status TESTS.md row; gh unauthenticated cause change) and 36134076882 (test_key_status.py hard-coded a Mac-only venv), each fixed at the source, not rebaselined. Workflow: daily cron 03:17 UTC + workflow_dispatch, all provider key variables emptied and unset, --source $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, receipt uploaded. EVAL c0b2f81.

title: Preflight: refuse a live run whose preregistered bar is unreachable (power/reachability check)
description: WHAT: A keyless checker, scripts/bar-reachable.py, that reads a prereg's arms from committed baseline/floor rows and computes the best achievable test result for the stated bar before any call. For paired McNemar: the maximum discordant pairs given the oracle headroom over the comparator on the exact prereg keys, and the smallest attainable p. For rate bars: the Wilson bound at a perfect score. Exit 1 when the bar cannot be met even by a perfect Jev arm; exit 0 with the numbers otherwise. WHY: jev-jjwt's prereg (c0ef4468) passed size and offered-answer feasibility, but its McNemar bar was unreachable (best single 22/24, max 2 discordant, p >= 0.5). Pane 1 caught it by hand; RULE 15 clause 4 names only size and offered-action checks. Emerald segment 2 (a523dc50) is the same class: its goal was solved by the prior. ACCEPTANCE: a unittest built on committed rows: jev-jjwt's 24-task split must exit 1 with max discordant 2; R112's 337-task two-archive split must exit 0 (b=2, c=8 showed room). A planted edit that drops the discordant computation must turn a test red. Registered in TESTS.md. Non-author check before close. No Jev call.

comments.author: AmberWillow
comments.text: NON-AUTHOR CHECK (pane 1) of 6e4ff307: tests OK in a clean clone; plant max_wins = tasks (drop comparator subtraction) -> 2 tests FAIL, restored byte-identical (cmp). One fail-open gap, not closed: mcnemar_reachability sets max_discordant_wins = tasks - comparator_exact (bar-reachable.py:147), which assumes Jev can complete every task the comparator misses. For a choice over fixed candidates (Best-of-N) the ceiling is the tasks where some offered candidate completes and the comparator does not (oracle headroom). Without it the gate says REACHABLE when no offered option can win. Fix: optional --oracle-exact (or per-task oracle rows) capping max wins at oracle_exact - both_exact, plus a test built from floor_receipt.json where the tasks minus comparator count exceeds the oracle headroom. Resume after the planning duel.
